title: Residency control gap assessment with Northgate Trust
next_steps: Samira to share SOC2 Type II report and key management whitepaper by 2029-02-09
Daniel to schedule a technical deep-dive for region-locked benchmark on 2029-02-14
Northgate to provide sample PII/data flow diagram by 2029-02-12
Set up trial Dedicated environment for pilot (scope: 2xA10s, EU-west region) pending procurement
action_items: Samira - send SOC2, HIPAA scoping note, and encrypted logs whitepaper - due 2029-02-09
Daniel - prep region-locked latency/cost baseline tests and runbook - due 2029-02-13
Javier - share internal network diagram and expected QPS profile - due 2029-02-12

meeting_header: Date: 2029-02-07 | Start: 14:30 UTC | Duration: 52 min | Attendees: Samira Patel, Daniel Cho, Priya Nair (Redwood) / Maria Liao, Tom Reynolds, Javier Morales, Renee Cho (Northgate Trust)
summary: Discovery focused on data residency constraints and logging controls. Northgate prefers region-locked hosting for EU customer data, strong controls around audit logs and key residency. Discussed hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs, KMS/HSM options, log redaction, and procurement timeline.
topics: Data residency requirements (EU-only for some datasets)
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private fit
transcript:
[00:00] Samira (Redwood AE): Hey everyone thanks for making time, looks like we have about 50 minutes. quick round of intros?
[00:10] Maria (Head of Cloud Ops - Northgate): Hi, Maria Liao here, I run ops for the trust side. we support client-facing services in eu and na.
[00:16] Tom (CISO - Northgate): Tom Reynolds, CISO, i'll be triaging compliance and risk.
[00:20] Javier (Platform): Javier Morales, platform eng, i'll handle network and infra details.
[00:24] Renee (Compliance): Renee Cho, compliance - HIPAA overlap and retention specialist.
[00:28] Daniel (Redwood SE): Daniel Cho, solutions engineer - i'll drive the technical fit and benchmarks.
[00:31] Priya (Redwood): Priya Nair, solutions architect - i'll help map controls to our architecture.
[00:35] Samira: Great. The call is scoped as a residency/control gap assessment. Maria, can you start with the hard requirements so we can map options?
[00:45] Maria: Sure. We have a split product set - some customers are EU-only by contract, some global. For the EU-only customers we need data at rest and logs to never leave eu-west. also, log access must be limited to our security team; third party access should be auditable and, ideally, logs redacted for PII. retention is 7 years for transaction logs per our legal.
[01:05] Tom: Also SOC2 is table stakes, but we also need evidence of key residency and separation. we run our own KMS for secrets, and we cannot export plaintext keys. So any vendor solution must integrate with our KMS or allow HSM key escrow in-region.
[01:22] Samira: Understood. Quick overview from us: Redwood supports three deployment modes — hosted (multi-tenant regional), Dedicated (single-tenant pools region-locked), and Private (VPC/on-prem). We can pin model serving to a region and enforce egress rules. For keys we offer customer-managed KMS integrations and optional customer HSM via private deployments.
[01:38] Javier: Question — with hosted, are the control plane and control plane logs leaving region? we need the control plane (meta, audit) to be able to stay in eu.
[01:45] Daniel: Good point. Our hosted control plane is global by default, but we do an enterprise offering that gives a private control plane in-region for Dedicated or Private customers. there are two flavors: control plane in-region, or fully customer-controlled control plane for on-prem. 
[02:00] Priya: To add, audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM (we support syslog/SQS/Azure EventHub) and you can restrict retention there. We can also stream sanitized logs to Redwood metrics for service health while keeping detailed logs in your storage.
[02:15] Renee: When you say sanitized, what fields do you redact? we need PII removed before logs leave the region.
[02:22] Daniel: The redaction layer can mask common PII (names, SSNs, emails) using pattern rules and custom regex you provide. note: automated redaction isn't perfect so there is a risk of leakage; for highest assurance customers we recommend Private deployment with no external egress.
[02:38] Tom: Ok. For onboarding we will need: SOC2 Type II, HIPAA attestation if available, encryption at rest and in transit details, KMS integration docs, and network topology. also, who has access to raw inference inputs? Our policy is that only internal service accounts may view full inputs.
[02:55] Samira: we'll share SOC2 and our security pack after the call. we can also provide a template NDA and data flow questionnaire.
[03:02] Maria: timeline wise procurement window is tight — pilot approvals in 4 weeks, production by end of Q2. cost is a factor; if Dedicated is too expensive we'll need to evaluate hosted with strict region locks.
[03:12] Daniel: We usually recommend Dedicated for predictable throughput and region controls. Hosted can be cheaper but requires extra contractual SLAs for region locking. We can run a cost comparison for your QPS and latency targets.
[03:25] Javier: Performance — some endpoints are extremely latency sensitive. if we move to Dedicated, what's the fallback if a zone has capacity issues? and can we route to a compatible quantized model?
[03:35] Priya: yes, smart routing can failover to a compatible variant in the same region. we also support burst policies to another region as a last resort but that would violate residency for EU-only data so you'd need canary rules: prefer region, fail closed or fail open depending on policy.
[03:52] Tom: Fail closed is our preference for EU-only sets. If a region is degraded we prefer returning 5xx rather than spilling data. that will affect SLA expectations.
[04:01] Samira: makes sense. We'll document the fail-closed option and the SLA implications.
[04:06] Maria: Logging access — we need role-based access with SSO (SAML/Okta) and audit trails. who in Redwood can see customer logs by default?
[04:15] Daniel: By default, only customer-designated service accounts can access logs. Redwood support can access logs under a documented escalation process and each access is logged. For Dedicated/Private we can disable Redwood support access entirely or require jump-boxes/audit justification.
[04:30] Renee: And for legal hold — if we need to put data on legal hold, how is that reflected in storage tiers and retention?
[04:36] Priya: We can mark objects with retention metadata and prevent deletion. For Private deployments you control the retention policy in your object store; for Hosted/Dedicated we can implement retention holds at the service layer and export evidence for audits.
[04:50] Tom: Key residency again — does Redwood hold any copies of customer keys?
[04:55] Samira: No, we have options: 1) Customer-managed KMS where Redwood never sees plaintext keys, 2) HSM-backed private keys in-region for Private deployments, or 3) For hosted we can do envelope encryption but keys may be in a partner KMS — which won't work for you.
[05:12] Javier: Encryption in transit — do you support mTLS between the model runtime and control plane?
[05:18] Daniel: Yes, we support mTLS and client certs for inter-service traffic in Dedicated/Private. Hosted also uses TLS but mTLS is an enterprise option for Dedicated.
[05:26] Maria: For the pilot we want a short list of acceptance criteria: region-locked serving for eu-west, no logs leaving region (sanitized metrics ok), KMS in-region integration, and latency under 150ms p95 for our baseline profile.
[05:40] Samira: We'll commit to providing a pilot spec and acceptance criteria doc. Daniel will run the benchmark and Priya will map controls to your compliance checklist.
[05:50] Tom: One more: can we get an architecture diagram that shows data plane vs control plane boundaries, and what telemetry is stored where?
[05:56] Priya: Yes — we'll include a diagram and a table enumerating telemetry fields and retention.
[06:02] Maria: Also interested in whether we can have a private peering connection or express route to avoid internet egress for initial handshake.
[06:09] Daniel: We support VPC peering and private link options to connect to Dedicated or Private endpoints. We'll include that in the network runbook.
[06:17] Renee: Are there any red flags you see from our initial ask?
[06:20] Samira: Nothing impossible, but two considerations: 1) hosted may require extra contractual measures to guarantee residency, and 2) redaction automation can miss edge PII cases — if absolute non-exfiltration is required, Private is the safe path.
[06:35] Tom: We're leaning Dedicated if costs are reasonable and if you can lock control plane in eu-west.
[06:40] Maria: procurement note — budget approval contingent on clear cost delta between hosted/dedicated and a committed discount for a 12-month reserved pool.
[06:50] Samira: We'll provide a pricing comparison and committed commitment terms for reserved capacity.
[06:55] Daniel: i'll put together a benchmark plan: data residency validation steps, latencies, and cost per token for your QPS.
[07:02] Samira: ok, any other quick questions?
[07:05] Javier: minor — do you support token-level logging off? can we disable request/response logging for certain endpoints?
[07:11] Daniel: yes, logging granularity can be configured per-route; we can set the inference endpoints to only emit minimal telemetry.
[07:18] Tom: good.
[07:20] Samira: recap of next steps: share SOC2 and security pack, schedule technical deep-dive, run pilot with Dedicated in eu-west, exchange network diagrams and retention requirements.
[07:30] Maria: thanks everyone, we'll aim to get the diagrams to you by Monday.
[07:33] Samira: great, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs. thanks all.
[07:38] (end)
